Christine’s father’s family were Russians of the Luga district, the lake-and-forest country south of Leningrad.
Germany invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941; Luga fell on 24 August after weeks of fighting,
and for two and a half years the district lay behind the German lines, between the siege of Leningrad and the partisans
in the forests. Germany’s war economy was short of workers, and from 1942 the occupiers sent Soviet civilians west
as Ostarbeiter, “eastern workers” — about 2.8 million in all, made to wear an OST badge and housed in camps.
As the front drew near in 1943 whole villages were emptied.
In March 1943 Valentin and Zinaida Maksimow and their children were taken from the Luga district to Germany and sent
to Weener, in East Frisia, near the Dutch border, nearly a thousand miles from home.
The Red Army retook Luga in February 1944.
